title: Model Selection & Benchmark Walkthrough — Nimbus Analytics
summary: Redwood AE + SE walked Nimbus through the model catalog filters, benchmark results spreadsheet, and compatibility matrix. Discussion focused on choosing open models for a mixed latency/throughput search reranking workload, quantization tradeoffs, and private deployment options (VPC). Next steps: share compatibility matrix + benchmark CSV, run 24h pilot with sample traffic, and follow up on pricing for Dedicated pool sizing.
topics: Model catalog filters: architecture, quantization, sequence length
Benchmark spreadsheet: p95 latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1M tokens
Compatibility matrix: model -> GPU family (A100/H100/L4) and runtime flags
Redwood Optimize recommendations: batching, prefix caching, KV cache
Security: VPC, KMS, SOC2 and data residency concerns
next_steps: Redwood to send model compatibility matrix (spreadsheet link) and raw benchmark CSV
Nimbus to provide 48h sample traffic and priority prompt set for pilot
SE to propose Dedicated sizing and estimated monthly commit
action_items: Marco Alvarez: export the compatibility matrix and attach H100/A100/L4 perf columns - due 2025-02-14
Laura Chen: send pilot T&C and pricing delta for Dedicated vs Hosted - due 2025-02-14
Maya Li: share example prompt set (50 queries) and expected SLOs - due 2025-02-18
questions: Priya: will Redwood support pinned model versions across Hosted and Dedicated?
Ethan: how does KV cache interact with rolling deploys and model rollbacks?
Maya: what's the latency impact of int8 quantization for our 1024-context reranker?
header:
Date: 2025-02-12 | Time: 16:00 PST | Duration: 48m
Attendees: Laura Chen, Marco Alvarez (Redwood) — Priya Sharma, Ethan Cole, Maya Li (Nimbus Analytics)
Recording: Fireflies.ai auto-record
Files shared: 2025-02-12-benchmarks.xlsx (link), model-compatibility-matrix.csv (link)
transcript: 00:00:02 Laura Chen: hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. i'm laura from redwood, joining with marco from solutions engineering.
00:00:10 Priya Sharma: hi laura, thanks. quick note, our times are tight so if we can focus on model selection and the benchmarks that'd be great.

00:00:18 Marco Alvarez: absolutely, we'll jump right in. goal today is to show the model catalog filters, the benchmark sheet we ran, and the compatibility matrix mapping models to GPUs and runtime flags.
00:00:27 Ethan Cole: perfect. we're most concerned about p95 latency for near-real-time reranking and cost per 1M tokens.

00:00:35 Marco Alvarez: makes sense. i'll share my screen — okay i have the console open, this is the model catalog. on the left side you can filter by architecture family, licensing (open vs proprietary), quantization support, and recommended gpu.

00:01:05 Marco Alvarez: you'll see an entry here, 'open-llama-7b' — note the catalog shows a recommended runtime profile: int8-ggml-style quant, but we also show experimentally measured p95 on A100 and H100 in the bench sheet.
00:01:22 Maya Li: just to confirm, these bench numbers are with our prompt shapes? or generic prompts?

00:01:28 Marco Alvarez: good question. the spreadsheet we're linking is generated from a suite we run with conversational and rerank-style prompts; it's generic but includes a tab for custom prompts if you want us to inject your 50 queries.
00:01:40 Priya Sharma: we'd like that — our reranker uses 1024 tokens context typically and we care about prefix cache behavior across requests.

00:01:49 Marco Alvarez: noted. the compatibility matrix column 'prefetch_kv' flags whether the runtime will preserve KV cache across requests for same session — some older models require a patch for continuous KV reuse, we call it 'kv-compat'.
00:02:05 Ethan Cole: i've seen docs where KV cache gets dropped on rolling deploys — is there a recommended pattern?

00:02:12 Marco Alvarez: yes, good thing to plan for. we recommend sticky routing on canary deploys or using our fallback policy which keeps the older model alive until the new model has warmed caches. we can show an example rollout config in the pilot.
00:02:30 Laura Chen: i'll flag that as an action item — marco will share the compatibility matrix and an example rollout snippet.
00:02:38 Priya Sharma: on quantization — we want to understand how int8 vs int4 changes quality for our dataset. do you surface eval delta metrics?

00:02:46 Marco Alvarez: yes, in the bench csv we include a 'quality delta' column which is the automated eval on a standard prompt set; it's noisy but gives direction. for many LLaMA-family models int8 preserves quality for reranking, int4 sometimes hurts at edge cases.
00:03:01 Maya Li: do you run the kernels on AMD instances or just nvidia? we use a mix of clouds and want to see L4 numbers too.

00:03:09 Marco Alvarez: primary tuning is on nvidia A100/H100 but we include L4-like results for cloud GPU inference (we call out MPS/TSM differences). L4 often shows better throughput on smaller models, but higher latency variability under bursty load.
00:03:26 Ethan Cole: what about batching? our traffic has microbursts — would batching add unacceptable tail latency?

00:03:33 Marco Alvarez: that's where Redwood Optimize comes in. we can tune batching windows; for microbursts we suggest dynamic batching with a max wait of 10ms to keep p95 low, and prefix caching to avoid recomputation for repeated prefixes.
00:03:49 Priya Sharma: can you explain the compatibility matrix columns? i'm seeing columns named 'runtime_tag', 'quant_support', 'recommended_gpu'.

00:03:57 Marco Alvarez: sure — runtime_tag is the runtime recipe (e.g., 'flash-attn-v2', 'kv-cache-stable'), quant_support shows tested quant modes like int8, int4, and any known regressions. recommended_gpu is our observed best fit for cost/latency.
00:04:12 Maya Li: is the recommended_gpu tied to single-token latency or tokens/sec throughput?
00:04:16 Marco Alvarez: we provide both — p95 latency with 1rps and tokens/sec at 64 concurrent requests. the bench sheet has a 'scenario' column to map to your workload.
00:04:29 Laura Chen: quick interjection — marco will call out H100 for larger 13b+ models for throughput, A100 for stable latency on many 7b series, and L4 for cost-sensitive small-serving clusters.
00:04:43 Ethan Cole: curious about rolling back — if we deploy a quantized variant and quality drops, what's the mechanism to revert quickly?
00:04:50 Marco Alvarez: you can pin route to previous model version. we also provide automatic rollback triggers based on eval alerts if your eval suite QoR drops beyond threshold.
00:05:03 Priya Sharma: can the console show token-level cost for a given route?
00:05:07 Laura Chen: yes, the Console shows token-level cost breakdown and per-route SLOs; it also shows cost by quantization profile so you can compare int8 vs fp16 cost delta.
00:05:18 Maya Li: we noticed in the bench spreadsheet 'openllama-7b-int8' had a 12% quality delta but cost 40% lower — any rule of thumb?

00:05:26 Marco Alvarez: general heuristic: if your reranker is precision-focused, prefer int8 with eval gating and keep fp16 fallback for mismatches. the Optimize tool can auto-suggest fallback policies by prompt cluster.
00:05:39 Priya Sharma: can you run a pilot that includes our prompt set to quantify that tradeoff?

00:05:44 Marco Alvarez: absolutely; if Maya shares the 50-query set we'll run a dedicated bench across selected models and quant settings and return CSV with p95, tokens/sec, and a small eval score delta.
00:05:55 Ethan Cole: curious about private deployments — our legal team wants VPC and KMS — is the catalog the same on Private?

00:06:02 Laura Chen: yes, the Private deployment uses the same control plane API and model catalog; you just configure the private control plane and KMS. we can include compliance docs in the follow up.
00:06:13 Maya Li: does Private support GPU burst to cloud if on-prem is saturated?
00:06:18 Marco Alvarez: hybrid bursting is supported with the Dedicated product line; we can route overflow to Redwood Hosted or a partner region with policy rules.
00:06:27 Priya Sharma: back to model selection — how do you recommend framing the search? we have a fairly mixed latency/cost objective.

00:06:33 Marco Alvarez: start with candidate families: LLaMA variants, Mistral-like, and smaller open models. filter for 'quant_support' and recommended_gpu, then use the bench CSV to compare p95 and tokens/sec at your target concurrency. we'll help you assemble a shortlist of 3 models for pilot.
00:06:52 Laura Chen: i'll also surface previous customers' patterns — many go int8 on small models and keep a fp16 fallback for edge cases.
00:06:59 Maya Li: any gotchas on the kernel side — e.g., flash-attn versions causing different latency curves?

00:07:05 Marco Alvarez: yes, the runtime picks kernels based on seq len and model shape; for some models flash-attn-v2 on H100 gives much better throughput but on A100 you might want an alternate kernel. that's captured in the 'runtime_tag' and a short note column in the matrix.
00:07:19 Ethan Cole: can you show the actual bench row for open-llama-7b-int8?
00:07:23 Marco Alvarez: sure i'm opening the spreadsheet — here: p95: 42ms on H100, tokens/sec 860, cost est $18 per 1M tokens. on A100 p95 48ms tokens/sec 700. quality delta -3% on our eval set.
00:07:40 Priya Sharma: 42ms p95 looks good. is that measured with prefix caching on?
00:07:44 Marco Alvarez: yes those numbers include prefix/KV cache enabled; without cache you'd see p95 jump by ~20-30% depending on request reuse.
00:07:55 Maya Li: what's the recommended batch size in those numbers?
00:07:59 Marco Alvarez: we used dynamic batching up to 8 tokens across 10ms windows in that scenario — it's annotated in the scenario column.
00:08:09 Priya Sharma: if we run the pilot, how do you ingest our traffic? do you need a VPN?

00:08:15 Laura Chen: simplest is a sample traffic export to S3 and we run the bench inside Redwood Dedicated or Hosted with your prompts. for Private/VPC we can set up a temporary peering or sftp transfer; we'll coordinate with Ethan on networking.
00:08:29 Ethan Cole: networking team will want an IP list and security contact. we'll loop them in after this call.
00:08:35 Marco Alvarez: understood — i'll include a networking checklist in the follow up with required ports and peering steps.
00:08:43 Laura Chen: quick note — from a pricing perspective, Dedicated commit sizes will change effective per-token rates; i'll include an example estimate for your expected 200M tokens per month.
00:08:55 Priya Sharma: rough estimate is 200–400M tokens monthly in production depending on adoption.
00:09:01 Marco Alvarez: we'll model cost for int8 vs fp16 scenarios and show projected monthly delta in the spreadsheet.
00:09:07 Maya Li: any SLA differences between Hosted and Dedicated?
00:09:11 Laura Chen: Dedicated includes SLA-backed uptime and latency targets plus support SLAs. Hosted is self-serve with best-effort and paid support tiers.
00:09:20 Ethan Cole: about compatibility — you mentioned some models need a runtime patch for kv-compat. how invasive is that patch?

00:09:26 Marco Alvarez: it's usually a small runtime shim that's applied at model onboarding; we handle that on Redwood side for Hosted and Dedicated. for Private we provide the patch and a short apply script.
00:09:37 Priya Sharma: excellent. any customer references who've used similar pilot patterns?
00:09:42 Laura Chen: yes we can share a short reference deck — i'll attach 1-page case study in the follow up.
00:09:48 Maya Li: ok next steps for us: we'll email the 50-query set and a sample of traffic logs. expectation is about 48h run, right?
00:09:55 Marco Alvarez: 24–48h depending on queueing; for thorough comparisons across GPUs we recommended 48h so we capture variability.
00:10:03 Priya Sharma: pausing for a second — is there any risk to data residency in Hosted during the bench?
00:10:09 Laura Chen: we can run the bench inside a region you specify; for sensitive data we recommend Private or Dedicated with VPC. we'll note that as part of the checklist.
00:10:20 Ethan Cole: ok great. anything else we should cover?
00:10:24 Marco Alvarez: maybe a quick look at the Console model route UI — i'll pull that up and show how to pin versions, set rollouts, and inspect token-level cost.
00:10:33 Marco Alvarez: (screen shows Console) here is a route config: you can set 'rollout: canary 5%' with fallback to 'fp16-model' and set eval alert thresholds that trigger rollback.
00:10:52 Priya Sharma: love that. can alerts post to our pagerduty?
00:10:56 Laura Chen: yes integrations include Slack, PagerDuty, Datadog — we'll include webhook setup steps in the follow up.
00:11:03 Maya Li: one last technical: how do you measure quality delta? is it BLEU or a custom metric?
00:11:09 Marco Alvarez: for reranking we use a combination: nDCG on held-out sets for ranking, plus a token-level logprob delta as a quick proxy. the CSV includes both columns.
00:11:21 Priya Sharma: ok that's useful. let's wrap and confirm the next steps.

00:11:26 Laura Chen: great — recap: Marco will send compatibility matrix + bench CSV, SE will run bench with your 50 queries once Maya uploads them, Laura will send pricing and pilot terms, and we'll schedule kickoff week of 2025-02-24. any objections?
00:11:42 Priya Sharma: none from me, sounds good.
00:11:45 Ethan Cole: same here.
00:11:47 Maya Li: good, thanks everyone.
00:11:50 Laura Chen: thanks all — we'll follow up with the spreadsheet and links. end recording.
